To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the FARIMA model is an effective tool for describing postural sway, and 2) the presence or absence (open vs. closed) eyes has a significant effect on the model parameter estimates, with the closed eyes case having the higher rms COP motion value, and the lower DC gain value.
the COP motion is modeled as an anti-persistent fractional random walk, and that the presence of vision affects the rms COP motion, the filter DC gain, and the Hurst exponent.

the postural sway of healthy adults can be characterized by a non-Gaussian FARMA process with an anti-persistent random walk component, that the Hurst exponent and the strength of the random walk component are affected by the presence or absence vision, and that the damping ratio and natural frequencies of the low-pass filter are affected by vision, but not the DC gain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of stochastic models for the COP motion, which is the result of a stochastic driving and a low-pass filtering mechanism.
the development of a stochastic model of the COP motion that can be used to predict its statistical characteristics.
the development of stochastic models of postural sway, which can be used in a statistical mechanical analysis of human postural control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the FARIMA stochastic models are useful for the analysis of postural data, and that they are able to account for many of the features of postural sway, e.g., long-range dependence, anti-persistence, and non-Gaussianity, and to explain the effect of the presence of vision.
, for the data analyzed, the presence of vision reduces the magnitude of the stochastic driving of the COP motion and increases the magnitude of the antipersistence of the COP motion.
, for healthy young subjects, the COP motion is a self-similar process with a Hurst exponent of 0.7, the rms COP time-difference motion is 2.5 mm and the DC gain of the filter is 1.0 mm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed modeling procedure is able to capture the non-stationarity of the COP data and to provide a quantitative measure of the postural control performance, which is a measure of the strength of the random walk driving.
the proposed model is able to describe the COP motion in terms of a few model parameters, and that the model parameter values are in good agreement with the results from the literature.
a non-Gaussian FARMA stochastic modeling approach is a useful tool for the analysis of human postural control.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a non-Gaussian FARMA stochastic model can capture the salient features of COP motion, such as: (i) the non-Gaussian nature of the time-differences; (ii) the antipersistent nature of the random walk process; and (iii) the low-pass filter effect on the random-walk process.
the COP motion can be described by the proposed FARIMA model, with the Hurst exponent as the most important parameter.

postural sway is best modeled as an anti-persistent random walk with a non-Gaussian FARMA filter, and that the Hurst exponent and the rms value of the time difference COP motion can be used as indicators of the presence or lack of visual feedback.
